creator: opichillc
title: Plain-English explainer of Jev, a non-chat decision model that returns structured choice/score answers with confidence for use in code

tools.name: Jev
tools.detail: New model type: you pass a question plus allowed answers; returns a pick/score plus confidence. Vendor not named in this video (TypeSafe AI per other videos)

claims: Jev cannot chat; it only answers when given a question and a fixed set of allowed answers
Three answer modes: likelihood (true/false-like), pick one from a list, score on a scale
Example: classify a customer reply as calm/frustrated/angry (1-3) and get back a score like 2.05
Every answer comes with a confidence score (e.g. 'angry' at 20% confidence can be routed to human triage)
Classification is 'almost real time fast' and the output is always consistently shaped for if/then code
Use cases: real-time lead-survey routing on free-text, chat routing, monitoring/alerting on messy input
how_to_steps: Send Jev the question plus the precise allowed answers (true/false, list, or numeric scale)
Receive a structured answer plus confidence
Branch in code on the answer and confidence (e.g. low confidence -> route to a human)
on_screen_only: Talking head only; no UI, URLs or docs shown
cta: Like and follow; comment whether this is hype or whether machine-to-machine models have potential

relevance.why: A cheap, fast, deterministic classifier with confidence is useful inside apps (routing, triage, gating agent actions), but this video is conceptual and vendor-agnostic.

implement_score.why: Worth an experiment only if a real routing/classification bottleneck exists; the same pattern can be done today with Claude Haiku + structured output, so test cost/latency before adding a vendor.

verify: Who makes Jev (TypeSafe AI?), API pricing, latency, and whether it is generally available
Benchmark Jev against Claude Haiku with JSON schema output on the same classification task
Is 'confidence' calibrated or just a softmax probability?
